# generate_playlist

[← Command index](README.md)

Write `.m3u` playlists for the media files in a directory tree.

## Synopsis

```
generate_playlist [options]
```

## Description

Two playlist types:

- `Tree` (default): one playlist at `-o` listing every matching file anywhere under
  the input directory, by absolute path.
- `Local`: for the input directory and each directory below it that directly holds
  matching files, a playlist named `<directory name>.m3u` inside that directory,
  listing those files by name only.

Entries are ordered by length and then alphabetically. Playlists that would be empty
or hold a single entry are not written unless `--allow_empty_lists` or
`--allow_single_lists` is given.

## Options

### Input/Output

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-i, --input_path <input_path>` | Directory to scan; must exist. |
| `-o, --output_path <output_path>` | Playlist file to write for `Tree`; not used by `Local`. |

### Selection

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-f, --file_types <file_types>` | Comma-separated file extensions to include, with the leading dot, e.g. `.mp3,.flac`. |
| `-t, --playlist_type <Tree\|Local>` | `Tree` writes one playlist for the whole tree; `Local` writes one inside each directory that holds matching files. Default: `Tree`. Allowed: `Tree`, `Local`. |

### Behavior

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `--allow_empty_lists` | Write playlists that have no entries instead of skipping them. |
| `--allow_single_lists` | Write playlists that have a single entry instead of skipping them. |

### Common options

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-v, --verbose` | Enable verbose mode. |
| `-p, --pretend_run` | Do a pretend run with no permanent changes. |
| `-x, --exit_on_failure` | Enable exit on failure mode. |
| `--no-preview` | Skip the preview confirmation prompt. |

## Examples

### Write one playlist for a whole music folder

```bash
generate_playlist -t Tree -i "/path/to/music" -o "/path/to/music/all.m3u" -f ".mp3,.flac"
```

### Write a playlist inside each album folder

```bash
generate_playlist -t Local -i "/path/to/music" -f ".mp3"
```

### Include several media types

```bash
generate_playlist -t Tree -i "/path/to/media" -o "/path/to/media/playlist.m3u" -f ".mp3,.m4a,.flac,.ogg"
```

### Also write empty and single-entry playlists

```bash
generate_playlist -t Local -i "/path/to/music" -f ".mp3" --allow_empty_lists --allow_single_lists
```

### Show which playlists would be written without writing them

```bash
generate_playlist -t Local -i "/path/to/music" -f ".mp3" -p -v
```

## Notes

- An existing playlist at the same path is overwritten.
